items.text: Vi gikk hele veien fra boulevarden og hjem, og han løftet hele tiden hånden – som om hånden hans var noe hellig folk skulle kysse.
items.q: Maman mocks her husband's holy airs after a pilgrimage. Does it sound like her?
Maman playfully speaks of herself by her family pet name, Nini. Does it sound natural?
before: Maman kniper igjen øynene og sier:

items.q: Maman doesn't know a doctoral defence has no grade and asks again. Does her question sound natural?

items.text: Hmm, vi tenkte at du ville bli opprørt, Nana-pesar-jan. Du hadde disputasen din.
items.q: Maman explains why the family kept sad news from her son. Does it sound like her?

items.text: Det er endetider. Bibis generasjon pleide å si at når endetiden kommer, fortsetter jorden å skjelve.
items.q: Maman, shaken by earthquake news, repeats what the old folk said. Does it sound like her?

items.text: Åh, Nana-pesar-jan, har du flyttet inn i den nye boligen din?
items.q: Maman asks her son on the phone whether he has moved house yet. Does it sound like her?
before: Omid ler, og jeg prøver å le med. Maman sier:

items.text: Er du frisk? Har du det bra?
items.q: Maman greets her son on the phone with a string of caring questions. Does it sound warm and natural?

items.text: Det er jo jeg som er stakkaren, jeg sier aldri noe, jeg holder alltid munn. Jeg ser bare på og spiser sorg.
items.q: She complains, half joking, that she always keeps quiet and swallows her sorrow. Does it sound natural?

items.text: Så kom sykepleieren selv og sa, jeg tror hun hører til dere.
items.q: Maman recalls a nurse at the hospital. Does this sound like her telling the story?

items.text: Uff, hver gang man ber ham hente noe, er det som om han får elektrisk støt.
items.q: Maman teases her son, who hates being sent on errands. Does it sound like her?

items.text: Siden det året du ble født har han sittet hjemme til nå.
items.q: Maman complains that her husband has sat idle at home for years. Does it sound like her?
Maman tells her little boy that salt is bad for him. Does it sound like a mother talking to a child?

items.text: Nei. Så lenge denne tråden er i hånden din, blir du ikke borte.
items.q: Maman comforts her small son with a game of thread. Does it sound like a mother talking to a little child?

items.text: Det får man når folk er glade for å se hverandre – ikke når de bare irriterer hverandre.
items.q: Maman says visits only earn God's reward when people are glad to see each other. Does it sound like her?

items.text: Den med den dumme læreren? Mm-hm, se den.
items.q: Maman encourages her son to watch a funny film. Does it sound like her?

items.text: Hmm, da sier jeg også at hjertet mitt blir tungt. La meg gå til venninnene mine.
items.q: Maman says she too gets lonely and wants to visit her friends. Does it sound like her?
